statement.p: Calculate the velocity and acceleration vectors, and speed for \mathbf{r}(t)=\langle \cos\mathopen{}\left(t\right),\sin\mathopen{}\left(t\right),\cos\mathopen{}\left(6t\right) \rangle when t=\frac{7 \pi}{6}.
Usage: To enter a vector, for example \langle x,y,z\rangle, type \lt x, y, z \gt

static.solution: \mathbf{r}(t) gives velocity: \mathbf{v}(t)=\mathbf{r}'(t)=\langle -\sin\mathopen{}\left(t\right), \cos\mathopen{}\left(t\right), -6\sin\mathopen{}\left(6t\right)\rangle and so velocity at t=\frac{7 \pi}{6} is \mathbf{v}(7 \pi/6)=\left\langle \frac{1}{2}, \frac{-\sqrt{3}}{2}, 0\right\rangle. Differentiating \mathbf{v}(t) gives acceleration: \mathbf{a}(t)=\mathbf{r}''(t)=\langle -\cos\mathopen{}\left(t\right), -\sin\mathopen{}\left(t\right), -\left(36\cos\mathopen{}\left(6t\right)\right)\rangle and so acceleration at t=\frac{7 \pi}{6} is \mathbf{a}(7 \pi/6)=\left\langle \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, \frac{1}{2}, 36\right\rangle. The speed is the magnitude of the velocity vector: ||\mathbf{v}(7 \pi/6)||=\sqrt{\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{-\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2+\left(0\right)^2}=1.
